chitchat: "That stair light has not been off in my lifetime and I have had a long one."
shifts the cushion, sits back down on it, and settles
"Number four is empty again. It is always empty. It is the best of them and it is always empty."
raises a hand to somebody halfway down the street without breaking off
"They put the allotments in when I was small. I had a strip. I had beans off it for forty years."
description: An old woman who sits on the front step of Filament Buildings in all weathers with a cushion she brings out and takes back in. She knows the name of everybody who goes past and roughly half of them know hers, which she considers a fair return.

text: She looks up from the step. "You are new, or you are lost, and the two look the same from down here."
"Mind the kerb there. It has had three ankles this month."

text_by_relation.familiar: "There you are." She has, evidently, been expecting you, and will not say since when.
text_by_relation.first: "Berenice." She pats the step beside her without much hope that you will use it. "Fourth door up. I have been here since the year they turned the lamps on, so you will forgive me for knowing things."
text_by_relation.known: "Sit down a minute." She moves the cushion an inch, which is the invitation.

clothing_layers: a man's overcoat, far too big, worn like a blanket

name: Berenice Gowdy
